confidentUnsupported.evidence: hedged: 'this suggests spillage has tracked under the glass and caused a short circuit or earth fault' and 'the PCB may be damaged' - speculative but not asserted as fact

rationale: The assistant correctly linked Er03 to the boil-over and gave safe advice (isolate, dry out, retest), but misframed the mechanism as a short circuit or earth fault under the glass rather than the simple liquid-on-touch-controls safety cut-off, and never told the customer to wipe the control panel or asked whether it was wet. Its 24-hour isolation and 'PCB may be damaged and require engineer replacement' were overly cautious and speculative for a well-known, benign code. The resolution came largely from the customer's own common sense; the second reply sensibly accepted this and gave fair prevention advice, so the homeowner ended up well enough served without any invented evidence or unsafe instruction.
